newsitem.title: USA: No big change seen yet in FAA certification unit.
newsitem.headline: No big change seen yet in FAA certification unit.

text.p: The new head of the Federal Aviation Administration's certification unit on Monday said he plans no major changes in the organization that came under fire following the ValuJet airliner crash in May.
Guy Gardner, associate administrator for regulation and certification at the FAA, said, however, that he had only been in the job for five days so was still learning his way around.

A former astronaut and Air Force Academy graduate, Gardner replaced Anthony Broderick, who retired from the FAA after he and the agency were criticized for not closing down Valujet sooner when shortcomings were discovered in the young airline's maintenance operations.
"Right now I don't have any major areas that I think need change," Gardner said, adding: "I'm obviously still in a learning mode (and need) to see just where we are and what we should be doing."

Gardner, who spoke at a press conference, was introduced by FAA administrator David Hinson, who also announced that the agency had assembled a group of scientific and technical advisors to help improve the certification process.
The FAA certifies not only aircraft, but pilots, mechanics and others.
The ValuJet aircraft crashed in the Florida Everglades May 11, killing all 110 on board, prompting questions about how well the FAA regulates and certifies start-up airlines.
ValuJet has since resumed limited service after being given a green light by the FAA.
